result:
Here's a draft. I wrote "suspected" because so far you've only seen the lag spike and the missing orders happen at the same time. Nobody has confirmed the lag caused the gap, and if the root cause turns out to be different, a title that states it as fact could send the investigation in the wrong direction. It still contains "Kafka consumer lag", so routing should work.

**Title:** Nightly order report missing ~1,200 orders, suspected Kafka consumer lag

**Description:** The nightly report for 2026-10-08 was missing ~1,200 orders, and the Kafka consumer lag dashboard shows a spike at the same time, so please investigate whether delayed consumption caused the report to run before those orders landed.

I assumed "yesterday" means 2026-10-08, so adjust the date if the report covers a different day. If you add the lag spike's start and end times, the data team can check them against the report's cutoff time.

If you'd rather have the stronger wording, "caused by Kafka consumer lag" is a one-word swap. I'd only use it once someone has confirmed the missing orders were still unconsumed when the report ran.
